name: ComCare Long Term Assistance (LTA)
summary: Long-term financial aid for those unable to work.
description:
ComCare Long Term Assistance (LTA) for those who are permanently unable to work. Provides monthly cash assistance, assistance with medical expenses at public healthcare institutions, free or highly subsidised access to social support services.

name: ElderFund
summary: Monthly cash aid for severely disabled elderly.
description: ElderFund is a discretionary assistance scheme launched on 31 January 2020. It is targeted at severely disabled lower-income Singapore Citizens aged 30 and older, who are not able to benefit from CareShield Life, ElderShield, and the Interim Disability Assistance Programme for the Elderly (IDAPE), and have low MediSave balances and inadequate personal savings to meet their long-term care needs. Eligible Singapore Citizens can receive up to $250 cash per month for as long as they remain eligible, and meet the terms and conditions needed for receipt of payment.
eligibility: Severely disabled Singapore Citizens aged 30 and older, not eligible for CareShield Life, ElderShield, or IDAPE, with low MediSave balances and inadequate personal savings for long-term care needs.
whatYouGet: Financial assistance for daily living expenses

name: Public Assistance Programme
summary: Monthly financial and food aid for needy families.
description:
- Individuals who are financially constrained or unemployed due to old age, sickness or disability, but are not eligible for government financial assistance.
- Low-income families with young children and/or family members who are elderly, disabled, sick or have special needs.
- Families which are adversely affected by unexpected circumstances, such as loss of breadwinner, permanent disability, etc.
eligibility:
Applicants must be:
- Individuals financially constrained or unemployed due to old age, sickness, or disability, and not eligible for government financial assistance.
- Low-income families with young children and/or family members who are elderly, disabled, sick, or have special needs.
- Families affected by unexpected circumstances (e.g., loss of breadwinner, permanent disability).
Applicants are assessed through home visits every 6 months. Referrals accepted from hospitals, family service centres, grassroots organisations, and public agencies.

name: Enhancement for Active Seniors (EASE)
summary: HDB’s EASE programme subsidises the installation of safety and accessibility features in HDB flats to help seniors and residents with mobility needs live safely at home. It provides items like grab bars, ramps, door widening, slip-resistant treatment, shower seats, and HFADs at subsidised rates.
description:
- Government-subsidised home modifications to improve safety and accessibility in HDB flats for seniors and those with mobility needs.
- Offered as part of the Home Improvement Programme (HIP) or via EASE (Direct Application) if the block is not due for HIP or if earlier installation is desired.
- Key improvements include:
  - Fall prevention and support: grab bars (various types), slip-resistant floor treatment, lowering of bathroom kerbs, wall-mounted foldable shower seat, handrail at main entrance.
  - Accessibility for wheelchair/commode users: single-step and multi-step ramps (portable or customised), wheelchair lifter (when ramps are not feasible), widening of toilet/bathroom entrances.
  - Safety and convenience: bidet spray, set of rocker light switches, Home Fire Alarm Device (HFAD).
- Highly subsidised costs with residents’ co-payment varying by flat type; items come with a 1-year warranty.
- Solutions are installed only where technically feasible; site assessments determine suitable items and any ancillary works (e.g., wash basin relocation, electrical upgrades).
eligibility: Singapore Citizen households (sold flats) and Registered Tenants (rental flats) may apply for EASE (Direct Application) if the household has a family member who is either: (1) aged 65 years and above; or (2) aged 60–64 years and requires assistance with at least one Activity of Daily Living (e.g., washing/bathing, dressing, feeding, toileting, mobility, transferring). Items are installed only where technically feasible.

name: Silver Housing Bonus
summary: Cash bonus for seniors who right-size to a 3-room or smaller HDB flat and commit to increasing their CPF RA for CPF LIFE payouts. Provides up to $40,000 per household depending on flat type and RA commitment.
description:
• The Silver Housing Bonus (SHB) is a cash bonus to help seniors who right-size to a 3-room or smaller HDB flat increase their retirement income.
• Seniors receive up to $30,000 when they commit up to $60,000 net increase to their CPF Retirement Account (RA) for CPF LIFE payouts after selling their existing home and buying a smaller flat.
• An additional $10,000 cash bonus is given when right-sizing to a 2-room or smaller flat, including a Community Care Apartment—bringing the maximum to $40,000 per household for eligible HDB owners, or up to $20,000 for eligible private property owners with AV between $21,000 and $31,000.
• The bonus is pro-rated based on how much is committed to the CPF RA, and can be fulfilled using CPF housing refunds (without cash top-ups if sufficient).
• It supports seniors to unlock housing equity, lower housing costs, and boost lifelong retirement payouts via CPF LIFE.
eligibility:
• Household: At least one owner is a Singapore Citizen aged 55 or above; gross monthly household income ≤ $14,000.
• Existing property: HDB flat (met MOP for resale) or private residential property with Annual Value (AV) up to $31,000.
• Property ownership limits: Must not concurrently own/hold interest in a private residential property, or own/hold interest in more than one non-residential property.
• Next property: Buying a 3-room (excluding 3-room terrace), 2-room or smaller HDB flat, or a Community Care Apartment.
• Net sale proceeds: Must be positive after accounting for outstanding loan, purchase price of next flat, resale levy (if applicable), and subsidy recovery (if applicable for Plus/Prime/PLH flats).
• Transaction timing: Book/buy the next flat before selling the existing property, or within 12 months after completing the sale.
• SHB commitment: Commit a net increase in CPF RA (capped at $60,000 and by the prevailing Full Retirement Sum) after right-sizing; funds may come from CPF housing refunds.
• HDB Flat Eligibility: Must meet HDB flat purchase eligibility and hold a valid HFE letter.
• Application window: SHB application within 1 year from the legal completion date of the second housing transaction; eligibility assessed at point of SHB application.

name: Singapore Red Cross' TransportAid
summary: Subsidised transport for low-income elderly and disabled.
description:
Singapore Red Cross’ TransportAid service helps the elderly and disabled from low-income homes get to and from their healthcare service facilities, such as medical treatments, rehabilitation and day activity centres. The TransportAid service is offered at subsidised rates, based on means testing results that are assessed by social workers.
 Call 6337 3333 or email us at transportaid@redcross.sg for more information or assistance on Transport Aid.
eligibility: Elderly and disabled individuals from low-income homes. Subsidy rates are based on means testing results assessed by social workers.

name: Community Health Assist Scheme (CHAS)
summary: Subsidies for medical and dental care at clinics.
description: Enables Singapore Citizens from lower- to middle-income households, and all Pioneers, to receive subsidies for medical & dental care at participating General Practitioners (GP) & dental clinics near their home.
eligibility: Singapore Citizens from lower- to middle-income households, and all Pioneers.

name: Medical Assistance
summary: Medical and dialysis aid for needy, disabled, elderly.
description:
Besides providing subsidies for medical expenses, the provision of medical supplies is also a major feature of our medical assistance programme. For long-term users who are struggling with their own limited financials, when the annual costs of their medical supplies constantly outstrip the limits of government grants and allowances, Tzu Chi will step in to fill the gap.

Volunteers sort medical supplies, such as adult diapers, waste bags, nutritional milk, etc. according to type, size, quantity, and home address, before personally delivering them to individual households during the monthly home visits.
eligibility: Needy individuals, including Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents, who are affected by illness or disability and require medical assistance. Renal patients must be assessed and referred by medical social workers or Sengkang General Hospital for specific programmes. Elderly kidney failure patients (age 60 and above) are eligible for the Renal Conservative Care Programme.
whatYouGet: Financial assistance for chronic or terminal illnesses
Financial assistance for assistive technology and medical equipment

name: Viriya Elderly Medical Programme (VEMP)
summary: VEMP supports low-income seniors with medical needs.
description: Help seniors with various medical conditions and who have low social and financial support. VEMP helps seniors cover their daily expenses. VEMP also helps the elderly cope with medical expenses including transport, TCM treatment and other consumables. Social work practitioners will work with eldercare agencies and hospitals to provide community care for the elderly. Case management services will also be provided to link the beneficiaries to the required community resources.

name: Matched Retirement Savings Scheme
summary: CPF matches retirement savings for eligible Singaporeans.
description: MRSS aims to help senior Singapore Citizens with lower retirement savings build up more. This will boost their monthly payouts in retirement. The Government will match every dollar of cash top-ups made to the RA of eligible members up to $600 per year.
eligibility: Eligibility is automatically assessed each year. Criteria: Singapore Citizen, age 55 and above as of 31 December of the assessment year (from 2026, also Singaporeans with disabilities below age 55), Retirement Account savings less than $106,500 (Basic Retirement Sum for 2025), average monthly income not more than $4,000, annual value of residence not more than $21,000. Must be a Singapore Citizen when the matching grant is credited. From 2025, no age cap (previously 70).
